## Intent
Hypothesis: scalar (non-vectorized) loop1 with branchy respawn is compute/overhead-bound rather than bandwidth-bound and cannot approach the streaming ceiling.

## Cache saturation
All measured N (4000–4M) exceed the L1d spill at N≈963, so the curve starts in L2. At q=0.01, cost FALLS from 8.364 ns/p (N=4000) to 8.078 (N=16000) — overhead amortization at small N. Crossing the L2 spill at N≈61680 produces no knee: N=65000 gives 7.912, and the curve stays FLAT through DRAM at 7.859 (N=262000) and 7.811 (N=1M), with a negligible uptick to 7.87 at N=4M. Raising death rate lifts the floor — q=0.05 plateaus near 8.53, q=0.25 near 11.2 — but preserves the same flat N-shape. The absence of any spill knee confirms the algorithm is not cache-limited; death rate raises the floor uniformly via branchy respawn overhead without altering the memory-access pattern.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.71 GB/s at N=1M, q=0.01 — 34.5% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. Bandwidth is flat across N at every death rate, confirming the algorithm is compute/overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound. The transition is by death rate, not N: q=0.01 holds ~34–35% of ceiling, q=0.05 drops to ~31.6% (7.97 GB/s), and q=0.25 collapses to ~24.2% (6.11 GB/s). The monotonic degradation with churn reflects rising branchy-respawn and scatter cost, not a memory-wall effect.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize. The sole vector-suffixed instruction is `movi.2d v10, #0` (register zeroing). All floating-point work is scalar on `s` registers: `ldr s0, [x25]`, `fmul s1, s1, s8`, `fadd s0, s0, s1`, `str s0, [x25]` — component-by-component within one particle, advancing by `#0x44` (68 bytes) per iteration. There is no gather; no `ld1` indexed load appears. Loop2 performs byte-granular scatter with scalar saturation: `ldrb w2, [x1]`, `add w2, w2, w12`, `cmp w2, #0xff`, `csel w2, w2, w11, lo`, `strb w2, [x1]` — 16 `strb` and 12 `ldrb` in the histogram. The spawn path contains a `udiv`/`msub` pair for index computation. This scalar codegen — 13 scalar `fmul`, 11 scalar `fadd`, 18 `csel`, 17 `cmp` — explains why bandwidth stalls at 34.5% of ceiling: the pipeline is instruction-throughput-limited, not memory-limited, and the byte-scatter in loop2 further serializes at higher churn.

## Verdict
Holds — the algorithm never exceeds 8.71 GB/s (34.5% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at q=0.01, and degrades to 6.11 GB/s (24.2%) at q=0.25, with flat bandwidth across all N confirming compute/overhead-bound behavior. The all-scalar codegen (zero vectorized FP, byte-granular scatter, scalar `udiv` in spawn) directly explains the gap to ceiling, validating that scalar loop1 with branchy respawn cannot approach streaming-bandwidth limits.
